scenes.text: Flip a switch and the light comes on instantly. So electrons must race through the wires, right? Not really.
In a copper wire, electrons drift on the order of millimeters per second. In one Georgia State University example, less than a third of a millimeter per second.
And with alternating current, the voltage swings back and forth 60 times a second, so the electrons mostly shuffle in place.
What travels is the energy, at essentially the speed of light. The full story is on The Hidden Grid.
